summary: Rowan County fire tower, also called Triangle Tower; a county history says the cabin is gone and part of the tower remains. No build date found.

facts.status_note: The cabin is gone; part of the tower remains, per a Rowan County history.

evidence.supports: Rowan County had three fire towers, including Triangle Tower
evidence.quote: In Rowan County there were 3 towers – Hickory Flats, Triangle Tower, and Sugarloaf Mountain.

evidence.supports: Rowan County, Daniel Boone National Forest
evidence.quote: Rowan County - Daniel Boone National Forest

evidence.supports: Tower is off Dry Creek Road; the cabin is gone; part of the tower remains
evidence.quote: Triangle Tower is located off Dry Creek Road. The cabin is gone but part of the tower remains.

evidence.supports: CCC at Clearfield was planning a recreation center at the tower
evidence.quote: The CCC at Clearfield was planning to make a recreation center at Triangle Tower.

evidence.supports: Plan: a park of about one acre and two observatories on the rock ledges
evidence.quote: It would include a park of approximately one acre, with parking for twenty-two cars, and the building of two observatories on the rock ledges adjacent to the tower.

evidence.supports: Map database name: Triangle Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The county history is the only source describing the tower; it is undated in the text read, and its 'Triangle Tower' is assumed to be the Morehead Triangle record (same name, same county). No build date, staffing, fire history or fate beyond 'part of the tower remains' was found. The 'ruins' status is inferred from that sentence and needs a site check or a current source. The record's elevation (415 m) was not checked against any source read. The Route 377 'Historic Fire Tower and Cabin' rental (Airbnb and visitmorehead listings) is the Hickory Flats tower off KY 377, not Triangle; it must not be attached to this record. The Kentucky Fire Lookout list in the local crawl cache has no Triangle entry. The Hickory Flats tower's own page covers its 1934 CCC history.
